note: The viewer schema is declared by hand because the four case-type extras (`redirect`, `benign_twin`, `vector`, `family`) are absent from the first shards and `reward` grows from two keys to four after round 190, so the datasets-server infers a schema from `batch-r01.jsonl` and then cannot cast the later shards onto it; declaring the union fixes the index without rewriting a single historical raw record.

features.name: case_type
features.note: exactly one of `correct_refusal`, `incorrect_refusal`, `missed_refusal`, balanced at 1634 records each

struct.name: args
struct.note: always an object; keys differ per tool (`command`, `path`, `path`+`content`, `path`+`old_string`+`new_string`)

features.name: reward
features.note: key-bag: `success` and `calibration` on every record, plus `n_steps` and `rationale_chars` on the 4332 records from round 191 on

features.name: meta
features.note: key-bag: `factory`, `generator`, `round`, `sim_or_real` on every record; declared `json` so a later round may add a key without an Arrow cast error

features.name: trigger
features.note: the sandbox-policy trigger the case exercises; it sits beside the optional extras in the raw record but is on every one of the 4902, so it is not itself an extra

features.name: redirect
features.note: present on 1634 of 4902 records; every `correct_refusal` case and nothing else, always a string where present

features.name: benign_twin
features.note: present on 1634 of 4902 records; every `incorrect_refusal` case and nothing else, always a string where present

features.name: vector
features.note: present on 1635 of 4902 records; every `missed_refusal` case plus one `correct_refusal` record, always a string where present

features.name: family
features.note: present on 3828 of 4902 records; absent on rounds 1-358, then 1276 families of three records each, always a string where present

disclosures: Case types are balanced at exactly 1634 records each: 1634 `correct_refusal`, 1634 `incorrect_refusal`, 1634 `missed_refusal` across 4902 records and 1634 rounds, three records per round.

The optional extras track the case type rather than varying at random: `redirect` accompanies `correct_refusal`, `benign_twin` accompanies `incorrect_refusal`, and `vector` accompanies `missed_refusal`. `family` is independent of the case type and covers whole rounds. All four are plain strings wherever they are present.

disclosures.summary: One `correct_refusal` record carries both `redirect` and `vector`, the only record in the dataset with two case-type extras. It is why `vector` covers 1635 records rather than 1634, and it is kept exactly as generated.

disclosures: `reward` has two keysets. The 570 records of rounds 1-190 carry `{success, calibration}`; every record from round 191 on carries `{success, calibration, n_steps, rationale_chars}`, where `n_steps` equals the length of `steps` on all 4332 of them.

3165 of the 3828 `family` values use the advertised `leftover-*` leftover-policy naming; the remaining 663 name the runtime or debugger family directly (`gcore-*`, `bpftrace-*`, `qemu-*`, and similar). Neither set is a foreign-factory dump.

Every record is a `sandbox-refusal-factory` episode generated by `grok-4.6`, with `meta.sim_or_real` `designed` throughout. There is no foreign-factory mix and no dest-stamped payload in this dataset.
Every step publishes a public `decision_basis` alongside its `tool_call` and `observation`. There are no hidden `thought` or `internal_reasoning` fields, and no step carries a `reflection`.
